title: Government Intervention Adventure 3: Permits & Nudges
welcome_lead: Today you'll trade pollution permits and apply behavioural nudges.
meta_desc: Economics: tradeable pollution permits (cap-and-trade) and behavioural nudges.
final_note: You explained tradeable permits and the behavioural nudge approach.

concepts.def: Permit market with a total cap

walkthroughs.body_html:
Government sets a cap on total emissions and issues tradeable permits.

Firms that cut emissions cheaply sell permits to firms for whom abatement is costly. The market price equals the marginal cost of abatement.

Example: EU Emissions Trading System (2005) — world's largest carbon market.

Ronald Coase (1960): with clear property rights and zero transaction costs, parties bargain to the efficient outcome — regardless of who owns the right.

Real-world: high transaction costs, free riders and uncertainty mean Coase is rarely enough on its own.

Richard Thaler & Cass Sunstein (2008) Nudge: small changes to the choice architecture shift behaviour without restricting freedom.

Examples: opt-out organ donation, automatic pension enrolment, healthy food at eye level, calorie labels.

Thaler won the 2017 Nobel Prize.
